rounds.text: Supershakti Metaliks Ltd trades at a compelling discount, marked by a price-to-book ratio of 0.87x against a book value of ₹ 258 per share [E2], and trades at 0.78x book value compared to a sector benchmark of 2.42x [E7]. The company is effectively debt-free with borrowings reduced to zero down from ₹ 19 Cr a year earlier, achieving a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E26, E28]. Profitability has surged remarkably, evidenced by a compounded profit growth of 116% over the trailing twelve months [E15] and a discounted cash flow intrinsic value pointing to a substantial margin of safety of 59.3% [E34]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's market price already implies an overly pessimistic -2.6% earnings growth [E35], ignoring the robust solvency profile reflected in a comfortable current ratio of 3.80x [E27] and steadfast promoter holdings of 72.23% [E30]. Conceded: the company carries negative operating and free cash flows for March 2026 alongside a low dividend yield of 0.22% [E4, E24, E25].

Supershakti Metaliks Ltd trades at a highly compelling valuation with a P/E ratio of 9.36x and a price-to-book ratio of 0.87x, both representing deep discounts compared to sector benchmarks of 21.43x and 2.42x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. The balance sheet has been successfully transformed into a fortress, with borrowings entirely eliminated down to Rs 0 Cr from Rs 19 Cr previously, yielding a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and strong short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 3.80x [E26, E27, E28, E39, E40]. Fundamental valuation models highlight extreme mispricing, as a discounted cash flow analysis reveals an intrinsic value of Rs 553 per share against the market price of Rs 225, creating a substantial margin of safety of 59.3% [E33, E34]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current share price absurdly prices in a -2.6% earnings decline, standing in stark contrast to the company's recent 116% surge in compounded profit growth and stable high promoter ownership of 72.23% [E15, E30, E35]. Conceded: the company faces headwinds from negative operating cash flow of Rs -4 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -8 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside a low 3-year median ROE of 7% [E19, E24, E25, E43].

Conceded: the company trades at a low P/E of 9.36x and P/B of 0.87x compared to sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7], and borrowings are reduced to Rs 0 Cr [E28, E39, E40]. However, that apparent valuation discount is heavily distorted by low-quality earnings, specifically a substantial other income injection of Rs 25.9 Cr [E45] alongside a flagged low tax rate [E42]. The bull's reliance on the DCF intrinsic value of Rs 553 [E33] and a 59.3% margin of safety [E34] ignores severe operational deterioration, highlighted by a -4% compounded sales growth rate over the trailing twelve months [E14] and deeply negative operating cash flow of Rs -4 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -8 Cr in Mar 2026 [E24, E25]. Furthermore, multi-year share price declines of -11% over 5 years, -21% over 3 years, and -29% over 1 year [E16, E17, E18] demonstrate that the market correctly discounts the firm's persistent low profitability, evidenced by a 3-year median ROE of just 7% [E19] and a low overall score of 57 out of 100 on the rules-based screen [E46]. Finally, the bull glosses over massive contingent liabilities totaling Rs 105 Cr [E44] and inconsistent operating margins over the last 3 years and 3 quarters [E21, E22] which undermine any confidence in sustainable long-term cash generation.
